options: A tiny living thing made of a single cell
A type of animal with lungs
A kind of rock or crystal
questions.explanation: A bacterium is a tiny, single-celled living organism - a whole living thing in one cell, without a nucleus.
questions.misconception: It's easy to think bacteria are miniature animals or plants, but they are their own kind of tiny single-celled organism.

options: It copies its DNA and splits in two (binary fission)
It needs a host cell to copy itself
questions.explanation: A bacterium reproduces by binary fission - it copies its DNA and splits down the middle into two identical cells.
questions.misconception: Reproduction that needs a host is how viruses work, not bacteria. Bacteria split in two on their own.

options: In soil, water, air, and in our bodies
questions.explanation: Bacteria live in almost every environment - soil, water, air, on our skin, and in our guts.
questions.misconception: Bacteria are not rare or only found in labs/hospitals; they are the most widespread organisms on Earth.

questions.prompt: Which statement about bacteria is TRUE?
options: Many bacteria are helpful, like those that digest our food or make yogurt
Bacteria can never survive outside a host
Bacteria are too big to live in soil
questions.explanation: Most bacteria are harmless, and many are helpful - they help digestion, make yogurt, and recycle nutrients - while only a small fraction cause disease.
questions.misconception: The idea that 'all bacteria are germs that make you sick' is the most common over-simplification; most are actually harmless or beneficial.
